name: Trace Rune
description: Draws a stable magical mark that carries a simple instruction, ownership sign, warning, or symbolic condition.

name: Spark Rune
description: Charges a small rune with a pulse of light, heat, sound, force, or signal on activation.

name: Holding Glyph
description: Preserves freshness, charge, chill, warmth, edge, or readiness within a marked object.

name: Pattern Sight
description: Reveals flaws in proportions, stress, geometry, copied sigils, and tampering in magical or crafted structures.

name: Imprint Script
description: Fixes writing, diagrams, maps, and formal text against casual forgery, erasure, or alteration.

name: Snare Rune
description: Creates a triggered glyph that blinds, shocks, marks, restrains, or otherwise punishes intrusion.

name: Bridge Rune
description: Projects temporary runic paths, stairs, footholds, or crossing geometry from marked anchors.

name: Relay Glyph
description: Links two or more runes so a signal, trigger, charge, or simple message passes between them.

name: Pattern Lock
description: Inscribes a lock or threshold that opens only to a defined phrase, gesture, bloodline, symbol, or sequence.

name: Engine Array
description: Builds a functioning runic system that powers repeated operations such as heating, lifting, sealing, filtering, signaling, or defense.

name: Severing Rune
description: Cuts the bond between magic and anchor, enchantment and target, spirit and vessel, or script and function.

name: Living Script
description: Creates an adaptive rune that rewrites parts of itself within set boundaries to respond to changing conditions.

name: Grand Inscription
description: Covers a large site with coordinated runic architecture so walls, gates, corridors, and devices behave as a unified magical system.

name: Law-Pillar Array
description: Raises standing inscriptions that define what may occur inside a zone: movement, speech, entry, violence, or spell-use.

name: World Inscription
description: The supreme runic working: the caster writes a temporary magical law into place itself, altering how a whole site behaves until the inscription is broken or rewritten.
